subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an explicit profile-level CLI reset requiring a safe Gateway restart as the supported recovery contract for early billing or usage-limit recovery?
rationale: The linked issue permits a CLI escape hatch but prefers automatic re-evaluation, and this PR creates a durable public command rather than repairing an already-defined CLI contract.

options.title: Sponsor the scoped CLI recovery
options.body: Accept the explicit profile reset as a bounded operator tool, contingent on inspectable live proof and refreshed checks.

options.title: Require automatic recovery
options.body: Keep the PR paused and implement provider re-evaluation or an in-product recovery path that does not require a shell and restart.

options.title: Keep existing expiry behavior
options.body: Decline the new command and rely on existing cooldown expiry or separately approved cooldown-policy changes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the scoped CLI recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the explicit profile reset as a bounded operator tool, contingent on inspectable live proof and refreshed checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the major auth-profile cooldown and persistence refactor work defining this product boundary.
